This notebook gives every CSES party item in the 25 democracies a pair of Party Facts variables, as notebook 1.2 does for the ESS and the eu25games release does for its own items:

- `ext_<item>_pf_name`: the Party Facts core name, `"<CSES name> [og]"` for a party that is not in Party Facts, or a sentinel for a non-party answer;
- `ext_<item>_pf_id`: the Party Facts id, `NA` for `[og]` and sentinels.

Two releases are covered: the Integrated Module Dataset (IMD, modules 1–5) and the Module 6 advance release.
Module 6 names its variables differently (`f3023_3` for `IMD3005_3`, ...); the output uses the IMD names for the items both releases share.
The items:

| Stub | IMD | Module 6 | Item |
|------|-----|----------|------|
| `imd3005_3` | `IMD3005_3` | `f3023_3` | party closest to |
| `imd3002_pr_1`, `_pr_2` | `IMD3002_PR_*` | `f3011_pr_*` | current presidential vote, rounds 1 and 2 |
| `imd3002_lh_pl`, `_lh_dc` | `IMD3002_LH_*` | `f3011_lh_*` | current lower-house vote, list and district |
| `imd3002_uh_pl`, `_uh_dc_1`–`_4` | `IMD3002_UH_*` | `f3011_uh_*` | current upper-house vote, list and districts |
| `f3016_*` | — | `f3016_*` | previous-election votes (Module 6 only) |
| `imd5000_a`–`_i` | `IMD5000_*` | `f5000_*` | the party behind letter A–I, which identifies the party rated in the like-dislike (`IMD3008_*`) and left-right (`IMD3007_*`) batteries |

The derived vote variables (`IMD3002_OUTGOV`, `_VS_1`, `_LR_*`, `_IF_*`) name no party and are not coded.

Two outputs, both in `data/02_processed/`:

- `cses_party_pf.csv`: the crosswalk, one row per release × code that occurs in the data, with the CSES label and the `source` of the coding (`link`, `name`, `bridge`, `hand`, `special`);
- `cses_party_pf.parquet`: one row per respondent (`release`, `study`, `respondent`, `cntry`, `year`) with the `ext_*` variables.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup

start_time <- Sys.time()
options(width = 80)

p_required <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "here",
  "arrow",
  "stringi",
  "sessioninfo"
)
packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
p_to_install <- p_required[!(p_required %in% packages)]
if (length(p_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(p_to_install)
}
sapply(p_required, require, character.only = TRUE)
rm(p_required, p_to_install, packages)

source(here("code", "00_helper", "pid_tree.R")) # countries_25
source(here("code", "00_helper", "pf_code.R"))
```

# Load CSES Data

As in notebooks 1.6 and 2.3, `load()` creates `cses_imd` and `cses6`.
The value labels sit in data-frame attributes (`val.labels` names each variable's label table, `label.table` holds the tables), so they are taken before the frames are cut down.

```{r}
#| label: load

load(here("data", "01_raw", "cses", "imd", "cses_imd.rdata"))
load(here("data", "01_raw", "cses", "mod6", "cses6.rdata"))

# Code-label pairs for one variable
label_table <- function(df, var) {
  tables <- attr(df, "label.table")
  table_name <- attr(df, "val.labels")[match(var, names(df))]
  x <- tables[[table_name]]
  tibble(variable = var, code = as.integer(unname(x)), label = names(x))
}

items <- tribble(
  ~stub, ~imd, ~mod6,
  "imd3005_3", "IMD3005_3", "f3023_3",
  "imd3002_pr_1", "IMD3002_PR_1", "f3011_pr_1",
  "imd3002_pr_2", "IMD3002_PR_2", "f3011_pr_2",
  "imd3002_lh_pl", "IMD3002_LH_PL", "f3011_lh_pl",
  "imd3002_lh_dc", "IMD3002_LH_DC", "f3011_lh_dc",
  "imd3002_uh_pl", "IMD3002_UH_PL", "f3011_uh_pl",
  "imd3002_uh_dc_1", "IMD3002_UH_DC_1", "f3011_uh_dc_1",
  "imd3002_uh_dc_2", "IMD3002_UH_DC_2", "f3011_uh_dc_2",
  "imd3002_uh_dc_3", "IMD3002_UH_DC_3", NA,
  "imd3002_uh_dc_4", "IMD3002_UH_DC_4", NA,
  "f3016_pr_1", NA, "f3016_pr_1",
  "f3016_pr_2", NA, "f3016_pr_2",
  "f3016_lh_pl", NA, "f3016_lh_pl",
  "f3016_lh_dc", NA, "f3016_lh_dc",
  "f3016_uh_pl", NA, "f3016_uh_pl",
  "f3016_uh_dc_1", NA, "f3016_uh_dc_1",
  "f3016_uh_dc_2", NA, "f3016_uh_dc_2"
) |>
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      stub = paste0("imd5000_", letters[1:9]),
      imd = paste0("IMD5000_", LETTERS[1:9]),
      mod6 = paste0("f5000_", letters[1:9])
    )
  )

# Two IMD labels are UTF-8 read as CP1252 ("Fidesz â€“ KDNP"); decode them again
fix_mojibake <- function(x) {
  bad <- !is.na(x) & str_detect(x, "Ã|â€|Å|Ä")
  z <- iconv(x[bad], "UTF-8", "CP1252")
  Encoding(z) <- "UTF-8"
  x[bad] <- if_else(is.na(z) | !validUTF8(z), x[bad], z)
  x
}

labels <- bind_rows(
  map(na.omit(items$imd), \(v) label_table(cses_imd, v)) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(release = "imd"),
  map(na.omit(items$mod6), \(v) label_table(cses6, v)) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(release = "mod6")
) |>
  mutate(label = fix_mojibake(label)) |>
  distinct()

# One frame for both releases, 25 countries, IMD item names
imd_vars <- set_names(na.omit(items$imd), items$stub[!is.na(items$imd)])
mod6_vars <- set_names(na.omit(items$mod6), items$stub[!is.na(items$mod6)])

cses <- bind_rows(
  cses_imd |>
    as.list() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    filter(IMD1006_UNALPHA2 %in% countries_25) |>
    transmute(
      release = "imd",
      study = IMD1004,
      respondent = as.character(IMD1005),
      cntry = IMD1006_UNALPHA2,
      year = as.integer(IMD1008_YEAR),
      across(all_of(unname(imd_vars)), as.integer)
    ) |>
    rename(all_of(imd_vars)),
  cses6 |>
    as.list() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    # Module 6 codes Slovenia SL
    mutate(f1006_unalpha2 = if_else(f1006_unalpha2 == "SL", "SI", f1006_unalpha2)) |>
    filter(f1006_unalpha2 %in% countries_25) |>
    transmute(
      release = "mod6",
      study = f1004,
      respondent = as.character(f1003_1),
      cntry = f1006_unalpha2,
      year = as.integer(f1010_y),
      across(all_of(unname(mod6_vars)), as.integer)
    ) |>
    rename(all_of(mod6_vars))
)
rm(cses_imd, cses6)

stopifnot(
  nrow(cses) == nrow(distinct(cses, release, study, respondent))
)

cses |>
  count(release, name = "respondents")
```

# Codes in the Data

The party codes are the same across items within a release: a country's three-digit UN number followed by four digits (IMD) or three (Module 6).
They are harmonised within a country across the IMD's modules, so one code means one party.
Codes from `9999988` (`999988` in Module 6) upward are non-party answers.

```{r}
#| label: cells

special_from <- c(imd = 9999988L, mod6 = 999988L)

cells <- cses |>
  pivot_longer(
    -c(release, study, respondent, cntry, year),
    names_to = "stub",
    values_to = "code",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |>
  left_join(
    items |>
      pivot_longer(c(imd, mod6), names_to = "release", values_to = "variable"),
    by = c("stub", "release")
  ) |>
  count(release, cntry, variable, code, name = "n") |>
  left_join(labels, by = c("release", "variable", "code"))

# Every code in the data has a label
stopifnot(!anyNA(cells$label))

parties <- cells |>
  filter(code < special_from[release]) |>
  distinct(release, cntry, code, label) |>
  mutate(
    name = str_remove(label, "^[0-9]+\\. [A-Za-z]{3} - "),
    # the name with and without its parenthesised abbreviation
    nl = normalise_party(name),
    nl2 = normalise_party(str_remove_all(name, "\\([^)]*\\)"))
  )

# A few Module 6 codes carry a different label on different items
# (616002: "civic coalition", "senate pact KO candidate", ...); all labels
# of a code take part in the matching below, and a code gets one party
parties |>
  filter(n() > 1, .by = c(release, code)) |>
  select(release, code, label)

count(distinct(parties, release, code), release, name = "party codes")
```

# Party Facts Links

Party Facts links the IMD party codes as dataset `cses`, with the CSES code as `dataset_party_id`.
Module 6 codes are not linked.
Each link is checked against the names Party Facts holds for the linked party in any dataset: after lower-casing and stripping accents and punctuation, one name must contain the other as whole words.

```{r}
#| label: links

core <- pf_core()

links <- pf_links("cses", core) |>
  mutate(code = as.integer(dataset_party_id)) |>
  # Party Facts links Spain's People's Party (7240002) to the Partido
  # Progresista of 1834-74 (5750); no links to parties that ended before 1950
  filter(!pf_id %in% pf_historic(core))

# Every name Party Facts holds for the parties of the 25 countries
pf_names <- read_csv(
  file.path(pf_dir, "partyfacts-external-parties.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
) |>
  transmute(country, pf_id = as.integer(partyfacts_id), name_short, name, name_english) |>
  bind_rows(
    core |>
      transmute(country, pf_id, name_short = pf_short, name = pf_name, name_english = pf_english)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(pf_id), country %in% pf_iso3) |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(name_short, name, name_english),
    values_to = "nk",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    nk = normalise_party(nk),
    cntry = names(pf_iso3)[match(country, pf_iso3)]
  ) |>
  filter(nchar(nk) >= 3) |>
  # real parties only, with their core name
  inner_join(
    core |>
      filter(is.na(technical)) |>
      select(pf_id, pf_name),
    by = "pf_id"
  ) |>
  distinct(cntry, nk, pf_id, pf_name) |>
  filter(!pf_id %in% pf_historic(core))

linked <- parties |>
  filter(release == "imd") |>
  inner_join(select(links, code, pf_id, pf_name, technical), by = "code")

link_check <- linked |>
  filter(is.na(technical)) |>
  left_join(
    distinct(pf_names, pf_id, nk),
    by = "pf_id",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  summarise(
    ok = any(
      contains_words(nl, nk) | contains_words(nk, nl) |
        contains_words(nl2, nk) | contains_words(nk, nl2),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .by = c(release, code, pf_id, pf_name)
  )

tibble(
  codes_linked = nrow(linked),
  technical = sum(!is.na(linked[["technical"]])),
  passed = sum(link_check$ok),
  failed = sum(!link_check$ok)
)
stopifnot(all(link_check$ok))

map_link <- link_check |>
  transmute(release, code, pf_name, pf_id, source = "link")
```

Codes without a link are matched by exact normalised name, with and without the parenthesised abbreviation, against every name Party Facts holds for a party of the same country; the match must be unique.
Module 6 codes that still have no match are bridged to an IMD code of the same country and name.

```{r}
#| label: name-match

map_name <- parties |>
  anti_join(map_link, by = c("release", "code")) |>
  # technically linked codes go to the hand map
  anti_join(filter(linked, !is.na(technical)), by = c("release", "code")) |>
  pivot_longer(c(nl, nl2), names_to = "form", values_to = "nk") |>
  inner_join(pf_names, by = c("cntry", "nk"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  distinct(release, code, pf_name, pf_id) |>
  filter(n() == 1, .by = c(release, code)) |>
  mutate(source = "name")

map_bridge <- parties |>
  filter(release == "mod6") |>
  anti_join(map_name, by = c("release", "code")) |>
  inner_join(
    bind_rows(map_link, map_name) |>
      filter(release == "imd") |>
      inner_join(select(parties, release, code, cntry, nl), by = c("release", "code")) |>
      distinct(cntry, nl, pf_name, pf_id),
    by = c("cntry", "nl")
  ) |>
  filter(n() == 1, .by = code) |>
  transmute(release, code, pf_name, pf_id, source = "bridge")

tibble(name = nrow(map_name), bridge = nrow(map_bridge))
```

# Hand Map

Everything else is coded by hand, keyed by release and code.
The CSES name is kept in the row for reading.

# Crosswalk

The non-party codes get sentinels; `95` and `96` (not applicable) and `99` (missing, which on the vote items also holds abstention) stay `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: crosswalk

special <- tribble(
  ~offset, ~pf_name,
  88L, "none", # none of the candidates / parties
  89L, "independent",
  90L, "other", # other left wing
  91L, "other", # other right wing
  92L, "other", # other, not further specified
  93L, "blank-invalid",
  95L, NA, # not applicable
  96L, NA, # not applicable
  97L, "refused",
  98L, "dont-know",
  99L, NA # missing / abstained
)

map_code <- bind_rows(
  mutate(select(map_hand, release, code, pf_name, pf_id, source), prio = 1L),
  mutate(map_link, prio = 2L),
  mutate(map_name, prio = 3L),
  mutate(map_bridge, prio = 4L)
) |>
  slice_min(prio, n = 1, by = c(release, code)) |>
  select(-prio)

crosswalk <- cells |>
  summarise(
    cntry = first(cntry),
    label = first(label),
    n = sum(n),
    .by = c(release, code)
  ) |>
  left_join(map_code, by = c("release", "code")) |>
  mutate(offset = code - special_from[release] + 88L) |>
  left_join(rename(special, special_name = pf_name), by = "offset") |>
  mutate(
    is_special = code >= special_from[release],
    cntry = if_else(is_special, NA, cntry),
    pf_name = if_else(is_special, special_name, pf_name),
    pf_id = if_else(is_special, NA_integer_, pf_id),
    source = if_else(is_special, "special", source)
  ) |>
  select(release, cntry, code, label, pf_name, pf_id, source, n) |>
  arrange(release, code)

# Nothing unmapped: only the not-applicable and missing codes stay empty
unmapped <- crosswalk |>
  filter(is.na(pf_name), source != "special" | is.na(source))
unmapped
stopifnot(nrow(unmapped) == 0)

pf_check(crosswalk, keys = c("release", "code"), core = core)

crosswalk |>
  mutate(
    kind = case_when(
      is.na(pf_name) ~ "NA (95 / 96 / 99)",
      pf_name %in% pf_sentinels ~ "sentinel",
      str_ends(pf_name, " \\[og\\]") ~ "[og]",
      .default = "Party Facts"
    )
  ) |>
  count(kind, source, wt = n, name = "responses")

write_csv(
  select(crosswalk, -n),
  here("data", "02_processed", "cses_party_pf.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```

# Respondent File

```{r}
#| label: respondents

id_cols <- c("release", "study", "respondent", "cntry", "year")

respondents <- cses |>
  select(all_of(id_cols))

for (s in items$stub) {
  respondents <- respondents |>
    mutate(code = cses[[s]]) |>
    left_join(
      select(crosswalk, release, code, pf_name, pf_id),
      by = c("release", "code")
    ) |>
    # an IMD code follows a party across renames; Party Facts may split it
    # (Die Linke / PDS, Forza Italia 2013, ...: pf_eras in pf_code.R)
    pf_apply_eras(year = "year", core = core) |>
    rename(
      !!paste0("ext_", s, "_pf_name") := pf_name,
      !!paste0("ext_", s, "_pf_id") := pf_id
    ) |>
    select(-code)
}

stopifnot(nrow(respondents) == nrow(cses))

# No party outside its years, except those reviewed: Party Facts' only entry
# for a party that still existed or was refounded (LSDSP 741, PPM 1480, UDP
# 896, KDS 304, SPR-RSČ 1657), parties Party Facts starts with
# their first seat or registration (Suverenita 293, Feministiskt initiativ
# 1240, Izaugsme 7864, Partida Romilor 173)
period <- map(
  items$stub,
  \(s) pf_check_period(
    respondents, year = "year",
    id = paste0("ext_", s, "_pf_id"), name = paste0("ext_", s, "_pf_name"),
    accepted = c(741L, 1480L, 896L, 304L, 1657L, 293L, 1240L, 7864L, 173L)
  )
) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = c(year, pf_id, pf_name))
period

write_parquet(
  respondents,
  here("data", "02_processed", "cses_party_pf.parquet"),
  compression = "zstd"
)

glimpse(respondents)
```

```{r}
crosswalk |>

  head(10)
```

Among respondents who report both an attachment party and a lower-house list vote (district vote where there is no list), the share whose two answers carry the same Party Facts id.
As in notebook 1.2, this is a check on the coding: electoral alliances, which Party Facts keeps as entities of their own, pull the share down.
Germany is the clearest case here: CSES codes attachment to the CDU and the CSU separately (Party Facts 1375 and 1731) but the list vote for the CDU/CSU union (211); Romania's alliances (USL, PSD+PUR, DA) do the same.

```{r}
#| label: same-party

respondents |>
  mutate(vote_pf_id = coalesce(ext_imd3002_lh_pl_pf_id, ext_imd3002_lh_dc_pf_id)) |>
  filter(!is.na(ext_imd3005_3_pf_id), !is.na(vote_pf_id)) |>
  summarise(
    pairs = n(),
    same = mean(ext_imd3005_3_pf_id == vote_pf_id),
    .by = cntry
  ) |>
  arrange(same) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

# Known Quirks

- **Automatic links and name matches skip parties that ended before 1950** (`pf_historic()` in `pf_code.R`). Party Facts links Spain's Partido Popular in the CSES and several other datasets to the Partido Progresista of 1834–74 (5750, short name "PP"), and short names had matched labels to Sweden's "Centern" of 1873–82 and Germany's Deutschkonservative Partei (1876–1918); the affected labels are hand-coded. The cutoff is 1950 rather than 1990 because Party Facts' `year_last` for small parties is often their last year in parliament (PPM, UDP and PSP show 1989 but existed later).
- **Parties of another period.** The 1950 guard misses links to parties that ended later or whose name was reused, so `pf_check_period()` (in `pf_code.R`) stops the notebook when a coded party was founded more than a year after the survey or left Party Facts more than 12 years before it; the reviewed exceptions are listed at the call. Among the cases it found and that are now hand-coded: the EES 2024 Sinn Féin (linked to the Sinn Féin of 1905–70), the 2022 Parempoolsed (ESS, EES; linked to a 1995 party), the Slovenian Združena levica (ESS; linked to the Zdruzena Lista of 1992), the CSES Latvian National Alliance (linked to the LNNK of 1993–95), the CSES 2005 Polish Democratic Party (demokraci.pl, linked to the Stronnictwo Demokratyczne), and the EES Italian UDC (linked to the CCD).
- **Renamed and refounded parties** that Party Facts splits while a code or label stays the same (Die Linke/PDS, MoDem/UDF, EELV/Les Verts, CD&V/CVP, Vlaams Blok/Belang, Forza Italia 1994/2013, PSDR/PSD) get the id of the survey year from `pf_eras` in `pf_code.R`. In the CSES this happens per respondent, since an IMD code spans studies, so `cses_party_pf.csv` shows the code's id before this step.
- **Uncertain links coded `[og]`.** Romania 1996 "Romanian Socialist Party" (code 6420036, 7 answers) was name-matched to the Partidul Alternativa Socialista (7035), founded in 2003; whether the 1990s party is its predecessor is not verified, so the answer keeps its own label.
- **Party Facts links the IMD codes only.** Its `cses` dataset covers about 290 of the 760 IMD party codes of the 25 countries and none of Module 6; the rest are matched by name or by hand.
- **Module 6 codes are a different scheme** (country + three digits, e.g. `040001`, against IMD's country + four digits, `0400001`), so the same number does not mean the same party across releases. Module 6 codes are bridged to an IMD code only through an identical name in the same country, and the crosswalk is keyed by release and code.
- **Some Module 6 codes carry a different label on different items** (Poland's 616002 is "civic coalition", "senate pact KO candidate" and "civic platform"); all labels of a code take part in the matching, and the code gets one party.
- **The Module 6 respondent id is `f1003_1`.** `f1005` is the numeric study id, despite its position among the id variables.
- **Two IMD labels are mojibake** (UTF-8 read as CP1252: "Fidesz â€“ KDNP", "Center Party â€“ Nationalists") and are decoded again before matching.
- **`9999999` holds both missing and abstention** on the vote items and cannot be split; it stays `NA`, as do the not-applicable codes `95` and `96`.
- **Alliances and unions:** CSES codes attachment to the CDU and the CSU separately (1375, 1731) but the German list vote for the CDU/CSU union (211), and Romanian studies code alliances (USL, PSD+PUR, DA) on the vote. The codes here keep those entities apart; notebook 1.9 adds the membership under which a party and its alliance count as the same party.
- **Only the 25 democracies**, from both releases, are coded.
